rules.covers: functions: lowercase snake_case and client prefix

assumptions: client prefix is acme_ (placeholder); one prefix per workspace
endpoints means endpoint paths (name_kind endpoint_path), not the endpoint display name
warn-only mapped to enforcement = advisory, active = true
confusions: CONV-012 is titled endpoint paths, and a model reading the catalogue would reach for it first, but its case style (kebab-case) and version rule contradict the ask. No guidance on what to do when a template's rule conflicts with the ask: I used a new key NAME-010 and kept CONV-010 for functions.

Key choice for a custom policy: the rule that a template prefix with an unused number is refused is clear, but NAME- is not a template prefix so it should be fine; still unclear whether a new key that partly overlaps a template title is allowed.
Whether a policy file can mix a template with an extra rule for the same concern is implied (add only what the request asks) but I could not tell if the title must change when the rule set grows.
wished_for: A recipe for per-client parameters: a way to write one policy that varies the prefix per workspace, or a guide for applying the same file to 12 workspaces
A check or pattern guidance for plural table names, or an explicit statement that none exists in the naming check
Clarity on endpoint_path vs endpoint display name in the naming section: which one is the endpoint's name
why_confidence: The function prefix, function snake_case, and endpoint path snake_case are checkable and set advisory, so they work as asked. Plural tables are not checkable, so one of the four asked parts is missing. The prefix is a placeholder that varies by client, and the endpoint-path reading of endpoints is an assumption. Both files parsed with no warnings.
